remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks. O'Keeffe wrote: "I live on a hilltop in a village.... From my eastern window the road out into the world seems to wind away far up and down. Nearby it seems to swoop under the house—then curves to the left instead and goes past me. The road winds along the foot of the hills at the edge of the mountains. A long dark mesa to the east—a ragged pink one to the west — a valley into the mountains to the south, then hills and a mountain to the north.... One day, playing with a camera, I tried to photograph the road and to get it all in I had to turn the camera at a very odd angle. My drawing—or painting—call it what you will—comes from that photograph" (*Some Memories of Drawings* [1988], unpaginated). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A thin band of pale pink twists diagonally across the canvas. Flanking the form on either side is a softly shaded background in tones of pink and green.
